classification.difficultyReason: Translate coin counts and total value into two equations, then eliminate a variable and interpret both counts.

content.prompt:
Solve this problem by introducing two pronumerals and forming two simultaneous equations, even though it can be done more easily using one pronumeral.

Toni’s piggy bank contains $\$19.20$, made up of 10-cent pieces and 20-cent pieces. If there are 114 coins in the piggy bank, how many coins of each denomination are there?

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the number of ten-cent pieces and $y$ the number of twenty-cent pieces. Express the total value in cents.

$$\begin{align*}x+y&=114 &&(1)\\10x+20y&=1920 &&(2)\\x+2y&=192 &&(3),\ (2)\div10\end{align*}$$

Subtract equation (1) from equation (3).

$$\begin{align*}(x+2y)-(x+y)&=192-114\\y&=78\end{align*}$$

Substitute $y=78$ into equation (1).

$$\begin{align*}x+78&=114\\x&=36\end{align*}$$

There are 36 ten-cent pieces and 78 twenty-cent pieces.

Check: $36+78=114$ coins and $10\times36+20\times78=1920$ cents, or $\$19.20$.
